parsed.explanation: π is defined only for finite prime-sets, and Claim 3.2's inference 'π(T)∈S_∞, so π(T) is a multiple of some π(t')' is an integer statement, so its proof covers only finite minimal transversals. Step 4(c) needs more: since Case B occurs at every stage, some member of C is disjoint from I∪Z_s for each s, so no I∪Z_s is a transversal; as every finite subset of I∪Z_ω lies in some I∪Z_s, every transversal contained in I∪Z_ω is infinite. Hence the minimal transversal extracted there by Zorn is infinite, and 'T∈C by (iii)' followed by 'Since T is finite' is not justified by Claim 3.2 as proven. No other passage establishes self-duality for infinite minimal transversals, and the finiteness theorem (hence Step 2 and the conclusion) depends on this step, so the gap is load-bearing.
